Shinylive – licence notice
==========================
Shiny apps run in this site in the way of Shinylive (Posit; https://github.com/posit-dev/shinylive),
which runs Shiny apps in a web page, with R in webR. The site's files below were written for the
workbench after Shinylive's code. They are not copies of it, but they follow its design closely –
the messages between the page, the service worker and the app's frame and their names
(configureProxyPath, makeRequest, openChannel, serviceworkerStart), the stand-in for the app's
WebSocket, and the calls into Shiny with which R answers the app's requests – and some parts are
near to Shinylive's own code:

  isolation-sw.js (its Shiny part)   after src/shinylive-sw.ts
  assets/js/shiny-socket.js          after src/shinylive-inject-socket.ts and src/messageportwebsocket.ts
  assets/js/shiny.js                 after src/messageporthttp.ts, src/messageportwebsocket.ts,
                                     src/messageportwebsocket-channel.ts and src/hooks/useWebR.tsx
  assets/js/rsession.js              its R functions wb$shiny_run, wb$shiny_reader, wb$shiny_http,
                                     wb$shiny_ws_open, wb$shiny_ws_msg, wb$shiny_ws_close and
                                     wb$shiny_tick: after the R code in src/hooks/useWebR.tsx,
                                     src/messageporthttp.ts and src/messageportwebsocket-channel.ts

(Compared on 15 October 2026 with Shinylive's main branch, commit
80eb17c461d6bfd60f61d16bef92ad9c83d87434.)

As far as these files derive from Shinylive, Shinylive's licence applies to those parts. Its
notice, from the file LICENSE of its repository, is reproduced here. (RStudio, PBC is now Posit
Software, PBC.)
